question: Does raising the speed reward raise the achieved reverse speed, now that v30 made a stable reverse gait possible?
gate: 10 s upright on 5 perturbed seeds AND |mean forward speed| >= 0.037 m/s (half the -0.074 command)
method: validate_backward_sustained.py, native MuJoCo, unchanged flat-terrain XML, motor slew limit on, 3 s warm-up, independent +/-0.02 qvel perturbations, command -0.074 m/s
conclusion: Raising the two speed-pressure terms by 2x and 4x changed nothing: -0.0281 -> -0.0290 -> -0.0251 m/s, all 5/5 stable. The reward pressure is therefore NOT the binding constraint on speed; the cap is structural (stride/foot placement geometry at this command), and the same terms that keep the robot upright appear to grip the stride rather than merely being under-weighted. Stability remains 5/5 across the whole sweep, so the stable endpoint is robust.
v33_next: Relax the contact/stability group itself (not the speed reward) to test the trade-off directly: backward_v33_relaxed (single 25 / swing 20 / shortfall 40) and backward_v33_released (10 / 8 / 20).
